mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals the Federal Reserve's shift to easing, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 20-day windows during easing periods, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day pre-easing average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of expected corporate cash flows, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 20-day windows after rate hikes, or 20-day returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day pre-hike average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals the Federal Reserve's shift to easing, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day forward returns in > 60% of 60-day windows during easing periods, or 60-day returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day pre-easing average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 20-day windows during strong labor growth, or 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 5-day pre-strengthening average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below 150,000 jobs signals a weakening labor market, which raises the cost of capital and reduces investor confidence, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 20-day windows during weak labor growth, or 20-day returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day pre-weakening average (t-test p > 0.05).

failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 20-day windows during weak supply growth, or 20-day returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day pre-weakening average (t-test p > 0.05).
